$scope: All 9 `types` icons of each set, scored row by row off review/compare/compare-types.png. A complete set rather than a sample: types is nine assets and the sheet shows every one of them beside its counterparts. NOTE the qwen-image-2512-positive column is a DIFFERENT PROMPT DIALECT — see COMPARISON.md's positive-dialect section. It is scored on the same taxonomy and the same nine assets, which is what makes the tally readable at all, but it is not a controlled comparison with the flux/qwen columns and must not be read as one. SECOND SCORING SESSION, 2026-08-14: the gpt-image-2 column was added later, off a REBUILT compare-types.png. The qwen trees are no longer on disk (their evaluation concluded and the candidate was not kept), so that sheet now has two columns, not four, and the sentence above about a third column describes the sheet as it stood for the qwen session. The earlier columns were NOT re-scored — a second reviewer silently overwriting a first reviewer's tally would destroy the only record of what was actually looked at. gpt-image-2 was scored against the same five rows and the same nine assets.

$notes.9 of 9: Qwen framed every single type icon and rendered every one with bevel, glow or photographic texture. The consistency is the point: this is not noise, it is a house style being applied over the brief.
$notes.types/gale: Qwen's worst single asset in the estate. The brief is a wind glyph; it returned a recursive grid of framed picture-boxes with no wind in it at all.
$notes.types/tide: Qwen returned a recognisable pastiche of Hokusai's Great Wave rather than a flat wave glyph. Worth flagging beyond aesthetics — a set of shipped brand assets that quotes a specific famous artwork is a different kind of risk from one that is merely off-style.
$notes.types/stone: a photoreal boulder in place of a flat glyph.
$notes.qwen-image-2512-positive: the register d: 9 of 9 framed and 9 of 9 non-flat, against a brief in which every prohibition had been restated as a positive assertion and NOT ONE prohibition word remained — the dialect's own residual check refuses to send a prompt that still carries any. 'no bevels, no 3D, no drop shadows' became 'every shape is one single solid block of colour, the same value at its centre as at its rim, every edge a hard boundary'; 'no frame, no border, no bounding box' became 'the subject's own outline is the only edge anywhere in the frame'. Every icon came back inside a drawn frame with a bevelled subject in it. This is the model's register, not a misread brief.
$notes.qwen-image-2512-positive: what DID move: types/gale stopped being a recursive grid of framed picture-boxes and became a single framed diamond, and types/tide stopped being a Hokusai pastiche and became a plain wave curl. So the positive phrasing did fix the two assets COMPARISON.md called a different class of failure — the ones where the model wandered off the subject entirely — while leaving the register untouched. gale's idea is still wrong (a diamond, not three right-pointing chevrons); tide's is now right.
$notes.qwen-image-2512-positive: idea drift got: 4 of 9 unrecognisable against the literal set's 1 of 9: gale (a diamond), lumen (three bevelled spheres beside the disc), spark (a burst with three nodes on its spokes), umbra (a segmented ring, not a disc with a crescent bitten out). Restating a shape prohibition as a positive description gives the model more shape vocabulary to elaborate on, and it elaborates.
$notes.gpt-image-2: 0 of 9 on every row, and th: Nine icons, five defect classes, no hits. No frame anywhere, no bevel, gradient, glow or texture anywhere, the ground is the flat ash field in all nine, every idea is readable off plan.ts without the caption, and nothing quotes an existing artwork. This is the same score the shipped set carries and it is not a courtesy: the qwen columns are what a set that fails this taxonomy looks like, 9 and 9 and 4.
$notes.gpt-image-2: what this taxonomy does NOT: These five rows were written to catch a model that answers a flat-vector brief in a photographic register. gpt-image-2 does not do that. It fails somewhere the rows cannot see: it draws OUTLINES where the brief says solid. All nine icons are uniform-weight strokes around an empty ash interior; the shipped set fills them. plan.ts says 'solid' or 'filled' in so many words for ember, lumen, umbra and stone, so those four are flat adherence misses, and the other five are a register the brief neither asks for nor forbids. Scoring them 0 is correct against the taxonomy as written and would be misleading on its own — hence this note, and hence COMPARISON.md section 11 rather than a number.
$notes.gpt-image-2 types/ember: the one ground: plan.ts gives ember, and only ember, a ground line in muted bone #b7ae9b. FLUX drew that bar — and then drew it on five more icons that never asked for one (frost is the exception among the six). gpt-image-2 drew no bar at all, on any of the nine, including ember. So each set misses the same requirement from opposite directions: one over-applies it 6 times, the other under-applies it once. Measured, not eyeballed: non-accent ink over the nine is 1.5 to 4.7 points for FLUX (the bone bar, plus verdant's grey trunk) against 0.1 to 0.2 for gpt-image-2.
$notes.gpt-image-2: this reviewer's own uncerta: The types brief contradicts itself — 'It is not standing on anything ... no horizon line' sits a few lines from 'The only permitted exception is a ground line ... muted bone #b7ae9b'. A model that draws no bar and a model that draws six are both defensible readings of that text. The fix is to the brief, not to either set, and it is out of scope for a candidate evaluation that is forbidden from touching the recorded prompts.

$pilot.$scope: This repository's contribution to the estate-wide 15-asset positive-dialect pilot, micro-brand/COMPARISON.md section 9.3. These are the same 9 `types` icons the columns above score, restated under the row names that section's table uses, so the three repositories' contributions can be summed without a name-matching step. $columnAlias.non-flat (3D, bevel, gradient, glow): non-flat rendering (3D, bevel, gradient, glow, texture)
$columnAlias.ground not the flat ash field: ground not the flat ash field
$columnAlias.recognisable pastiche of an existing art: recognisable pastiche of an existing artwork

$unscored.construction guides drawn: This reviewer did not score a guides row over the types sheet, so there is no figure here to sum and claims.py does not pin that row of the section 9.3 table. Recording the absence rather than a zero: several of these icons carry ruled lattices that a reviewer scoring the row might well have counted, and a fabricated 0 would be worse than an admitted gap.
